segments.text: You ask AI, what should I name my new dog?
It suggests Spot.
You start a new chat and ask the exact same question.
This time, it suggests Max.
Why did the same question get a different answer?
Three main components dictate an AI's response.
First, the specific model you use
and its processing time.
Second, what the AI receives,
your prompt and provided context.
But the third column is where the real mechanics live.
AI uses techniques giving different tokens a chance,
sampling and temperature.
Because the model, the inputs
and these internal probability mechanics
interact differently in every session,
the AI builds each response dynamically
based on choices made in the moment.
Take a look at this probabilities chart.
The AI has generated the phrase, you could name him
and is evaluating its options for the next open blank.
Right now, Spot leads the starting odds at 22%.
You might expect the AI to pick the winner automatically.
But a 22% probability means AI would pick Spot
about 22 times out of 100 dries,
on average, if the odds stay the same.
That's called sampling.
If we run five separate random picks
with these exact unchanged probabilities,
we get a specific sequence.
Pick one, Max.
Pick two, Spot.
Pick three, Buddy.
Pick four, Rex.
And pick five, Max.
Spot was picked only once,
even with the highest probability.
Another five picks could turn out entirely differently.
Because the AI uses probability as a frequency guide
rather than a strict mathematical rule,
the exact same underlying state
will naturally produce varying outputs
across different attempts.
Why does AI work this way?
Choosing the absolute most likely token every single time
makes the AI's answers rigid, predictable,
and highly repetitive.
Giving other likely tokens a chance to be selected
introduces essential variety.
It makes the generated text feel more creative
and natural to a human reader.
And these choices compound.
Choosing a different token for just one blank
immediately shifts the context,
shaping what comes next
and sending the rest of the answer
in an entirely different direction.
Incorporating this probabilistic selection
is a deliberate choice that allows the system
to mimic the dynamic, varied nature
of human thought in conversation.
Sampling selects a token using probabilities.
Temperature adjusts those probabilities.
In chatgbt, Gemini, and Claude,
temperature is set behind the scenes.
This chart compares how different temperature settings
change the odds for each dog name.
Notice the center column.
These are the starting odds derived directly
from the model's training and the context you provided.
A low temperature setting concentrates the odds
onto the most likely choices.
Spot leads at 22%, but at low temperature,
its chance jumps to 36%.
A high temperature setting does the opposite
by spreading the odds out more widely.
Here, spot's chance falls to 16%.
Both settings manipulate the exact same starting odds.
And that bottom other category is simply combining
the hundreds of remaining low probability vocabulary words.
Spot remains the most likely individual token
at all three settings.
Temperature changes its probability.
Temperature acts as a focus style,
tightening or loosening the AI's adherence
to the most predictable path.
But it never overwrites the core understanding.
AI answers vary.
Different inputs, different odds, different choices.
